hardware_summary: Two boilers aboard the FSRU Excellence (Excelerate Energy, IMO 9252539, built 2005), fired on boil-off gas, integral to the vessel's own power supply while moored and regasifying — a July 2026 fire that damaged the power/control cabling connected to those boilers forced a suspension/reduction of gas send-out, confirming the boilers (not shore power) run the terminal.
source_notes: Moheshkhali is served by Excelerate's FSRU Excellence, moored offshore (floating=True, offshore=True) with a subsea gas pipeline to shore but no shore power cable. The vessel's two boilers, run on boil-off gas, supply the FSRU's own electrical power for regasification pumps and other loads. A fire on 21 July 2026 'severely damaged critical power, control and instrumentation cables connected to its two boilers,' forcing a nationwide gas-supply cut of roughly 450 mmcfd while repairs (imported spare parts, UK/UAE technical teams) were arranged — direct evidence that the terminal's operation depends on the boilers' own power output rather than any external supply. No source discloses a specific MW rating for this vessel; general FSRU-conversion technical literature describes boil-off-gas-fired power plants in the 15-25 MW range built for exactly this purpose (running regasification units and other onboard loads).

hardware_summary: 2 x 10 MW-class gas turbine generators onboard the FSRU (1 operating + 1 standby), natural gas (BOG/vaporized LNG) as primary fuel with HSD as secondary fuel, described in the project EIA as a 'captive power generation facility at site.'
source_notes: The Summit LNG FSRU (moored offshore at Moheshkhali, off-grid by construction) generates its own onboard power via gas turbines fed primarily by boil-off/vaporized LNG (HSD as backup fuel), sized to the vessel's ~10 MW load with 1 operating + 1 standby unit for redundancy. The project's own EIA explicitly labels this a 'captive power generation facility.'

hardware_summary: On-site fuel-gas-fired energy system at the Lumut plant ('equivalent to a 300 MW power station', 9 steam boilers fired on fuel gas incl. recovered BOG) driving both turbine-compressors (mechanical drive) and generator turbines (electricity); co-located with this is the 246 MWe Lumut Cogen Power Station, gas-fired, commissioned 1987, operated by Brunei LNG Sdn Bhd itself, supplying electricity and steam to the plant's industrial operations.
source_notes: Brunei LNG's Lumut plant runs its own on-site, fuel-gas-fired energy system (nine steam boilers, described by the operator as equivalent to a 300 MW power station) that drives both the liquefaction trains' turbine-compressors and generator turbines. The co-located 246 MWe Lumut Cogen Power Station is operated by Brunei LNG Sdn Bhd itself and supplies electricity and steam to the site.

source_notes: The Bauhinia Spirit FSRU (world's largest FSRU, 263,000 m3, delivered 2023) is a self-contained, self-propelled vessel whose own onboard dual-fuel generators supply its electrical loads, including the five regasification units that vaporize the cargo before send-out. hardware_summary: 18 MW gas-turbine-based captive power plant (CPP) -- the terminal's primary power source, with Gujarat State grid (66 kV, from a substation ~10 km away) as standby, and an emergency diesel generator as a further backup for CPP-and-grid failure.
source_notes: Chhara LNG Terminal's Risk Assessment / EIA report (filed by HPCL/HPLNG with India's environmental clearance authority) states the terminal's power will be supplied from an 18 MW captive power plant (CPP) using a Gas Turbine Generator, with the Gujarat State 66 kV grid as standby supply and an emergency diesel generator for CPP+grid failure. Heat recovered from the GTG exhaust also feeds an LNG vaporizer (STV) heat-recovery loop.

hardware_summary: Three (3) gas-turbine generator (GTG) packages forming Petronet's own on-site captive power plant at the Dahej terminal, running on regasified natural gas; a diesel genset is provided only for black-start of the gas turbines. Media reporting (not independently verified this pass) puts existing capacity at roughly 25 MW.
gogpt_plant: DGEN Mega Combined Cycle power plant
source_notes: Petronet's Dahej LNG terminal has its own on-site captive power plant: a technical bid/procurement specification document explicitly names 'three (3) GTG packages' as 'the captive power plant of Dahej LNG Terminal,' fired on regasified natural gas, with a diesel genset provided only for black-start of the gas turbines (not as the main power source). This is a primary operator/EPC technical specification, sufficient alone for green. Media reporting (Reuters; not independently verified this pass due to bot-blocking with no cached snapshot) additionally describes an existing ~25 MW captive plant at Dahej, and a much larger, separate 1,200 MW gas-fired commercial power project later proposed for the same site -- that larger unit is not itself confirmed built and is not part of this captive finding.

hardware_summary: Three 9.6 MW gensets (29 MW total) based on 20-cylinder Rolls-Royce Bergen B35:40 gas engines, delivered by Rolls-Royce under a full EPC contract for Dhamra LNG Terminal Pvt Ltd (DLTPL) to meet the terminal's baseload power requirement.
source_notes: Dhamra LNG (Adani Group / TotalEnergies JV, DLTPL) contracted Rolls-Royce in June 2020 for a complete EPC-delivered 29 MW gas power plant -- three 9.6 MW gensets on Bergen B35:40 gas engines -- explicitly to meet the LNG regasification terminal's own baseload power requirement, with over 98% reliability. This is on-site, dedicated generation for the terminal itself, not a supply to an external plant.

source_notes: Petronet LNG's proposed Gopalpur terminal (Phase-I: 4 MMTPA FSRU-based; Phase-II: 5 MMTPA land-based) includes 'GTGs for captive power' as a named Phase-II design element in its Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change Terms of Reference (ToR) letter dated 03/07/2023. hardware_summary: On-site captive gas turbine generator (GTG) plant, 13 MW, supplying part of the terminal's power alongside grid import; separate 1.6 MVA diesel emergency DG set for backup (non-gas, informational only).
source_notes: Kochi LNG Terminal (Petronet) is partially self-powered: a 13 MW on-site captive gas turbine generator (GTG) plant supplies part of the terminal's electricity, topped up by Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) grid power. A separate 1.6 MVA diesel emergency DG set exists purely for backup (diesel, not gas, so not itself a captive-gas finding but confirms the GTGs are the gas-fired plant).

hardware_summary: Gas-fired boilers raise steam for a steam turbine that drives the LNG train refrigerant compressor (mechanical drive, currently being studied for replacement by a PLN-grid-fed 160 MVA electric motor drive — conversion not yet complete). Separately, a 13.4 MW gas turbine at the Badak LNG plant is documented in the plant's own 'Equipment Technical Data Book' (1998), cited in a 2021 peer-reviewed power-augmentation case study by a PT Badak NGL engineer — a paper topic (inlet-air-cooling power augmentation) applied to generation-duty gas turbines, consistent with an on-site gas turbine generator.
source_notes: PT Badak NGL (Bontang LNG) currently runs its refrigerant-compressor steam turbine on steam raised by fuel-gas-fired boilers — an on-site gas-fired mechanical drive system — and separately maintains at least one 13.4 MW gas turbine per its own 1998 equipment data book (cited in a 2021 power-augmentation study). PT Badak is in early-stage discussions (MOU signed Sept 2023 with PLN, feasibility study only) to replace the steam-turbine compressor drive with a 160 MVA PLN-grid-fed electric motor — i.e. a partial migration toward grid supply that had not been completed as of the source date, so the gas-fired drive remains the documented current arrangement.

hardware_summary: Mixed-refrigerant and propane-cycle gas turbines drive the refrigeration compressors across the LNG trains (mechanical drive; described as 'heavy-duty gas turbines' in Baker Hughes' long-term service scope); exhaust heat from these gas turbines is recovered via Heat Recovery Steam Generators (HRSG) driving steam turbines that generate electricity, used on-site and with surplus historically sold to PLN (4 MW cited for a village-electrification program). Exact turbine model/count and total generating MW not disclosed in sources found.
source_notes: Confirmed on-site power generation via waste-heat recovery: the Tangguh Expansion Project (Train 3) ESIA states IFC Performance Standard 3 (resource/energy efficiency) 'is met with the installed heat recovery system using the off-gas from the gas turbines as energy input. Produced electricity is used internally and sold to Indonesia's state electricity company PLN.' This is a partially-captive, mixed mechanical-drive + power-generation site: mechanical-drive gas turbines run the refrigeration compressors, and their waste heat generates electricity used on-site (captive) with the surplus exported to PLN.

hardware_summary: Dual-fuel (gas/diesel) auxiliary generator set aboard the FSRU (vessel: Karunia Dewata), fitted with a SOGAV (Safety of Gas Admission Valve) fuel-gas supply system feeding the generator's cylinders -- a DFDE-type (dual-fuel diesel-electric) marine auxiliary power plant; count/rating not disclosed in the source.
source_notes: The FSRU Karunia Dewata carries its own onboard Dual Fuel Generator (DFDE-type, gas/diesel) providing the vessel's electrical power; a 2025 maritime-academy thesis documents a fuel-gas-supply fault (SOGAV/gas admission valve) in this generator during a May 2022 incident at Benoa Port, confirming gas-fired operation. No MW nameplate is disclosed. This is separate from the terminal's send-out relationship to the Pesanggaran Diesel and Gas Power Plant (PLTDG), which is an external grid power station the terminal supplies (not captive).

hardware_summary: Wison New Energies standard FLNG design (Genting/Kasuri West Papua FLNG uses this platform): Gen-1 spec = 2x LM6000PF+ aeroderivative gas turbines (with waste-heat recovery) mechanically driving the refrigerant compressors, plus an LM2500 aeroderivative turbine driving NGL-recovery booster compression, plus Solar Titan 130 aeroderivative gas turbine generators (with WHR) for power generation.
source_notes: West Papua FLNG (Kasuri, PT Layar Nusantara Gas / Genting Oil) is being built by Wison New Energies on Wison's standardized FLNG platform, whose published design includes both mechanical-drive turbines for refrigeration compression (LM6000PF+, LM2500) and dedicated gas-turbine generators (Solar Titan 130) for site power -- both gas-fuelled, both on-site, on a moored offshore facility with no grid connection.

hardware_summary: 2x MHIET KU30GA natural gas engines, 5,500 kW each (11,000 kW / 11 MW total generation capacity), gas-engine cogeneration installed 2004; retrofitted in 2018 with Miller-cycle combustion and a switch from micro-pilot-oil ignition to spark ignition, further reducing residual liquid-fuel dependence.
source_notes: Hiroshima Gas installed an 11,000 kW (2x 5,500 kW) natural-gas-engine cogeneration plant at its Hatsukaichi factory in 2004 specifically to power the LNG terminal's own refrigeration/vaporization load, with waste heat recovered as hot water for LNG vaporization (cutting vaporization fuel gas use by ~60% per the announcement) and surplus power (~10,000 kW) wheeled to the grid for wholesale sale. This is on-site gas-fired electricity generation whose primary purpose is powering the terminal — a captive, partially-exporting plant, and stays green even with the grid-export component per SOP.

hardware_summary: On-site gas turbine generator plus a diesel generator, both installed as non-normal-time (emergency) electrical power sources in addition to the two-line utility grid feed. No count/model/MW disclosed.
source_notes: INPEX's Naoetsu LNG terminal carries an on-site gas-turbine generator as one of two emergency/non-normal power sources (the other is diesel), backing up the dual utility grid feed. No MW figure or model is publicly disclosed, but the existence of on-site gas-fired generation is documented by the equipment vendor.

hardware_summary: 3x 5,500 kW gas-engine cogeneration units (16,500 kW total), commissioned Oct 2 2017, at Toho Gas's Yokkaichi Works (四日市工場)
source_notes: Toho Gas built a 16,500 kW (3x5,500 kW) natural-gas engine cogeneration plant at its own Yokkaichi Works, commissioned Oct 2 2017, explicitly for internal use: balancing the plant's own power demand fluctuations ("需給調整用の電源") while waste heat feeds the on-site city-gas manufacturing process. This is on-site generation whose stated purpose is powering/heating Toho Gas's own works, not grid sale.

hardware_summary: Yoshinoura Multi-Gas-Turbine plant, 35,000 kW, multi-fuel (LNG primary, kerosene, bioethanol), commissioned Mar 20 2015, at Okinawa Electric's Yoshinoura site
source_notes: Okinawa Electric's 35,000 kW Yoshinoura Multi-Gas-Turbine plant (commissioned Mar 20 2015, LNG-primary multi-fuel) has FOUR documented duties: (1) island-wide blackstart power if all of Okinawa loses power, (2) explicit security/backup power ("保安電源") for the LNG fuel tank at Yoshinoura thermal power station when that station loses power, (3) peak-demand response power in normal operation, and (4) BOG processing. Duty (3) means it carries real load in normal service, and duty (2) directly powers/secures the LNG terminal's own tank systems, so this is captive power under the SOP — category power_generation per the 'carries load in service' rule (not standby_backup) given its normal peak-power duty.

hardware_summary: 4x GE PGT25+G4 aeroderivative gas turbine generator systems (power generation) + 2x LM6000-PF+ 2BCL907 aeroderivative gas turbines in mechanical-drive mode driving the nitrogen-train compressors, supplied under GE Oil & Gas's Nov 2014 turbomachinery contract for PFLNG DUA.
source_notes: PFLNG DUA (Dua FLNG Terminal), a moored offshore FLNG vessel, carries 4x PGT25+G4 gas turbine generator systems supplying the facility's electric power and 2x LM6000-PF+ 2BCL907 aeroderivative gas turbines mechanically driving the nitrogen liquefaction-train compressors. Both were installed under GE Oil & Gas's November 2014 turbomachinery contract for FLNG Dua.

hardware_summary: GE-supplied gas turbines comprising both the plant's power-generation units and its liquefaction-train (refrigerant compressor) drivers across the Bintulu complex (MLNG, MLNG Dua, MLNG Tiga). Pre-2024 the complex relied 'solely on gas-powered turbines' for electricity; a 2024 grid tie-in (Project GLORY) substitutes only 40% (90 MW) of PLC's total power requirement with Sarawak-hydro electricity, leaving the remaining majority of house power gas-turbine-generated. Train-specific Frame-turbine models/ratings for MLNG Dua were not found in a citable primary source this pass.
source_notes: The PETRONAS LNG Complex (PLC) at Bintulu -- which includes MLNG Dua (Trains 4-6) -- generates its own electricity on gas-fired turbines. Petronas's own 2024 account states the complex was 'relying solely on gas-powered turbines' for power before a new 90 MW grid tie-in (Project GLORY, completed ~Q4 2024) substituted 40% of total site demand with Sarawak hydro-electricity, leaving the majority still gas-turbine generated. GE's separate service-contract press release confirms its maintained gas turbines 'comprise the power generation units and liquefaction trains' across MLNG, MLNG Dua and MLNG Tiga -- i.e. both electricity generation and mechanical-drive compressor trains.

hardware_summary: 2× GE Frame 7EA gas turbines (mechanical drive, each paired with a 13-megawatt induction motor running VSI/VSD technology at 3,600 rpm) driving Train 9's low/medium-pressure mixed-refrigerant and propane/high-pressure mixed-refrigerant compression trains; Train 9 is part of the wider Petronas LNG Complex (PLC), which Petronas states 'traditionally relies on fuel gas to power operations, with gas-powered turbines generating electricity on-site' (complex-wide, not train-specific MW disclosed).
source_notes: Train 9 has 2 GE Frame 7EA mechanical-drive gas turbines (13 MW motor-assisted each) driving its refrigerant compression trains — a captive (mechanical-drive) gas installation. The wider Bintulu complex Train 9 belongs to is also confirmed by Petronas to generate a portion of its own electricity on-site via gas turbines (partially captive: Project GLORY now substitutes ~40%/90 MW of the complex's power with Sarawak Energy grid hydro, leaving the balance on-site gas generation).

hardware_summary: GE-supplied gas turbines comprising both dedicated on-site power-generation units and liquefaction-train mechanical drives are covered under GE's 2016 US$127.6M long-term service agreement, which explicitly names MLNG, MLNG Dua, and MLNG Tiga as the three facilities served (existing GEM ref, reconfirmed). Petronas separately states the wider Bintulu complex 'traditionally relies on fuel gas to power operations, with gas-powered turbines generating electricity on-site' (now partially substituted, ~40%, by Sarawak Energy grid hydro under Project GLORY).
source_notes: MLNG Tiga is one of three facilities (with MLNG and MLNG Dua) named in a GE long-term service agreement covering 'all GE-supplied gas turbines and related equipment that comprise the power generation units and liquefaction trains for the LNG complex' — i.e. both on-site electricity generation and mechanical-drive liquefaction turbines. Petronas' own electrification article confirms the wider complex has traditionally self-generated its power via on-site gas turbines, partially substituted (not replaced) by grid hydro since 2024.

hardware_summary: PFLNG SATU (moored at the Kanowit gas field, off-grid by construction): GE supplied '4 of its PGT25+G4 gas turbine generator systems' (electricity generation) plus '2 PGT25+G4 gas turbine driven compressor units' (mechanical drive) and '2 electric motor driven centrifugal compressors modules' for the liquefaction process — GE's compression trains are described as vital elements of the liquefaction process.
source_notes: PFLNG SATU is a moored FLNG vessel (off-grid almost by construction, per the grid-access prior) with 4 GE PGT25+G4 gas turbine generator sets providing on-site electricity generation, plus 2 more PGT25+G4 units in gas-turbine-driven mechanical-drive mode for compression, alongside 2 electric-motor-driven compressor modules — a mixed generation + mechanical-drive site.

hardware_summary: Purpose-built onshore gas-fired power plant at Sipitang (Sabah), adjacent to the Sipitang Oil and Gas Industrial Park (SOGIP) where PFLNG Tiga will be moored nearshore: 7× MAN Energy Solutions 20V35/44G gas engines, 70 MW total capacity, explicitly described by both MAN (equipment vendor) and Riviera Maritime Media (independent trade press) as becoming the SOLE electricity supply to the nearshore FLNG terminal. As-designed captive power on an under-construction facility (per SOP, this counts).
source_notes: PFLNG Tiga (nearshore FLNG, under construction, commercial ops targeted 2027) will draw its entire electricity supply from a dedicated, purpose-built decentralised gas power plant at Sipitang: 7 MAN 20V35/44G gas engines totaling 70 MW, described as the 'sole supply of electricity' to the terminal — i.e. a dedicated (not merchant-grid) captive arrangement, even though the genset island sits onshore adjacent to the mooring rather than on the vessel hull itself.

RE-VERIFY, OVERTURNS PRE-EXISTING TRUE. Chana LNG Terminal is an onshore LNG import/storage facility with pipelines built specifically to feed the adjacent Songkhla Chana 1.7 GW gas-fired combined-cycle power plant (KOWEPO/TPIPP/KOGAS JV, signed March 2021), whose electricity output is sold entirely to EGAT (the national grid), not consumed on-site by the terminal. This is the classic direction-test case: the terminal supplies gas OUT to an external power plant (already correctly captured in GEM's PowerPlantsSupplied = 'Songkhla Chana power station'); it is not powered BY a captive plant. No source anywhere describes on-site captive generation for the LNG terminal itself.
